Translate hydro locations between networks

Source: R/translate.R
translate_hydrolocations.Rd

Places points that are indexed to one network (NHDPlusV2, NHDPlusHR, or 3DHP) on the flowlines of another, keeping each point on the mainstem it is on in the source network. The mainstem comes from the point's source identifier, not from its geometry, so a point near a confluence stays on its own river.

translate_hydrolocations(
  x,
  from,
  to,
  method = c("geometry", "hydro_location"),
  search_radius = units::set_units(1000, "m"),
  precision = 10
)

Arguments

x

sf POINT data.frame with the source identifier column for from (comid, nhdplusid or id3dhp) or a mainstem_uri column.

from

character network x is indexed to, one of "nhdpv2", "nhdphr", or "3dhp".

to

character network to place x on, one of "nhdpv2", "nhdphr", or "3dhp".

method

character "geometry" or "hydro_location". See details.

search_radius

units distance passed to index_points_to_lines, in a linear unit since indexing is in EPSG:5070. Only flowlines of the point's own mainstem are searched, so the radius can be wide enough to span differences between networks, such as a reservoir that one network routes differently from another.

precision

numeric meters, passed to index_points_to_lines. Lines near each point are segmentized to this spacing so the match is to the nearest point on a line, not the nearest vertex; NA matches vertices only.

Value

x with mainstem_uri, id (target flowline), id_measure, offset, past_end_km, status, method, and measured_on added, and for "hydro_location" also hydro_location_id and distance_km.

Details

The mainstem of each point comes from, in order: a mainstem_uri column on x; for "3dhp", a mainstemid column; otherwise the identifier column for from (comid, nhdplusid or id3dhp), looked up in the ref_rivers tables (see add_mainstems) or the 3DHP flowlines. A superseded mainstem (see check_mainstems) is reported and not placed; update_mainstems resolves it.

The target flowlines of each mainstem come from get_mainstem_flowlines. There are two ways to place a point on them.

method = "geometry" indexes the point to the target flowlines of its mainstem with index_points_to_lines and aggregate_ids. offset is the distance from the point to the target flowline.

method = "hydro_location" indexes the point on the source flowlines, records it as a distance from the nearest confluence that both networks have on that mainstem (get_confluences and add_hydro_location_distance), and lays the distance out on the target (index_hydro_location_distance). The placement is approximate in absolute terms but stays on the same side of the confluence, which is what matters for upstream drainage. offset is the distance from the point to the source flowline.

status is one of: placed; not_placed (no flowline within search_radius); no_mainstem; mainstem_superseded; mainstem_not_in_target (no target flowlines for the mainstem); and, for "hydro_location", no_shared_hydro_location (no confluence on the mainstem is in both networks, so the point is known only to be on mainstem_uri), past_end and hydro_location_not_in_x as described in index_hydro_location_distance. measured_on names the target network and the ref_rivers release, or for 3DHP the range of featuredate. 3DHP identifiers are not persistent, so a 3DHP placement holds for that release.

Points and flowlines are indexed in EPSG:5070 (CONUS Albers), so offset is in meters.

The ref_rivers lookup tables are large downloads on first use (see add_mainstems), so this function has no example.


# a point on New Hope River just above the Northeast Creek mouth
pt <- sf::st_sf(comid = 8894344,
                geometry = sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(-78.9763, 35.8355)),
                                      crs = 4326))

translate_hydrolocations(pt, "nhdpv2", "3dhp", method = "hydro_location")
